challenge.geowords: three app-generated words per round from the approved review words of block 3 sections 1-8, three words from three different sections; letters on the countries map of Asia with its rivers

prompt.object: the country or river name as on the cards; no capitals, records or facts

speedHunt.order: difficulty alternates easy, medium, easy, hard… (random inside a tier, no object repeats within a round); after a tier runs out the others go on in turn
speedHunt.correct: +1 and the next object at once
speedHunt.wrong: the right place lights up for 0.5 s; no penalty except time; the object goes into the weak list
speedHunt.hit: a river counts within 8 CSS px of its drawn line; a country counts inside its outline or within 22 CSS px of it; the small countries (the hard tier) within 36 CSS px — an enlarged tap area that lies only over the sea, never over a neighbour: a tap inside another country's outline answers that country (only a tap within 2 px of the asked country's own border line still counts for it), and the nearest object of the pool wins, so two enlarged areas never overlap

excluded.why: mountains, lakes, deserts and section-1 places are on other maps (no time to switch maps in 60 s); no capitals: their dots are too small on the map of Asia for a timed game

speedHunt.score: objects found in the round + personal best

stars.note: the same as Europe; tune after testing with children

geowords.words: approved review words (role review) of data/dictionary/b3-section-1..8.json, each word once; three different sections per round; recently played words last
geowords.places: the whole countries map of Asia: the 49 countries (a letter in the main part of the country, its circle wholly inside the border; on the whole map of Asia only the largest countries can hold the circle, the others take no letter), the 23 rivers («on the Mekong») and a river inside a country it crosses («on the Mekong in Cambodia»), the four lakes drawn on the map (Caspian, Aral, Balkhash, Issyk-Kul) and the section-1 objects (not the Arctic Ocean, Chukotka or the Bering Strait); at least a third of the letters on rivers, then the lakes, seas, islands, peninsulas and countries first, so a word is never rivers only; a country named once; spacing 10% of map width (at 9 two letters' tap areas can overlap on the whole map)
geowords.fallback: a word that cannot be laid out is replaced by the next word of another section
